title: Short Stuff: Vomitoria
summary: Short Stuff episode debunking the myth that ancient Romans routinely binged and purged in designated vomitoria. The hosts explain that a vomitorium was really an architectural passageway in the Colosseum (Macrobius used the term in the fourth century CE) for moving crowds in and out of seats. The myth traces to Aldous Huxley's comic novel Antic Hay (1923), and Lewis Mumford repeated it in The City in History. The hosts then discuss real modern vomitoriums in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, and a beer hall in Munich, Germany, and the unsourced "puke pants" claim from a HowStuffWorks article. The episode closes with a Trainspotting tangent and the sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and the peanut butter myth
segments.summary: The hosts open with banter and introduce the claim that ancient Romans ate huge amounts and vomited in a designated public area to keep eating. Josh says it is not true and admits he had repeated the myth on the show before.

segments.title: What a vomitorium really was
segments.summary: Macrobius used the term in the fourth century CE for passageways into and out of amphitheaters like the Colosseum. The hosts describe the Colosseum's 76 entrances, which let about 50,000 people reach their seats in roughly 15 minutes.

segments.title: Aldous Huxley and Lewis Mumford spread the myth
segments.summary: Aldous Huxley's 1923 novel Antic Hay mentions a goth entering a vomitorium, which appears to be the first use of the term for vomiting. Lewis Mumford later cited it as fact in The City in History.

segments.title: Real vomitoriums in Vietnam and Germany
segments.summary: Real vomitoriums exist in Ho Chi Minh City, where some have Roman imagery. A beer hall in Munich, the Hofbräuhaus, has one. The hosts question a HowStuffWorks claim that German frat houses call them puke pants, which they could not verify.

segments.title: Trainspotting tangent
segments.summary: The hosts joke about bathroom vomit and discuss the Trainspotting toilet scene before moving on.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact info
segments.summary: The hosts tell listeners how to get in touch through the website and the email address.
